summary: This excerpt from Book 4 (part 114) follows Valentine in a starving, war-stricken city. Her mother Mata returns after three weeks in hospital with her broken bones mended, and the family reunites with the silent younger boy Trover, who has grown tall enough to hug Valentine at the waist. Valentine cannot sleep, so she takes a glowing light from her galosh on a secret night walk, and the passage closes with the bread ration cut to 120 grams and her growing hunger.
one_line: Valentine's mother returns from hospital to a famine-stricken city, and Valentine's hunger and quiet secret walks deepen.
key_facts: Valentine's mother came home after three weeks in hospital, where she had her broken bones mended.
Mata entered the flat moving like an old woman, and Valentine cried while hugging her.
Silent Trover had grown tall enough to hug Valentine at the waist instead of the knees.
Mata took a painkiller in pill form, which were now everywhere in the city.
Valentine kept a pea-sized glowing light in the toe of her single winter galosh, kept inside a grip sheet parcel under her bed.
The other galosh had been stolen the winter before while Valentine had both off to warm her toes before returning to digging.
Valentine took the glowing light outside into the hot night to light a secret walk through the old streets.
Nine months after her father died, winter had sent autumn as a threatening envoy.
The bread ration was cut to 120 grams, and there were sometimes pebbles in the bread to increase its weight.
Valentine and the other diggers cursed the enemy, not the city, when the bread was bad.
The narrator notes that no one had it any better and that everyone fought and suffered together.
Valentine is so hungry all the time that she observes you cannot eat pride.
In a queue for bread, a man old enough to be an elder snatched Valentine's ration and fled, as the passage ends mid-scene.
The passage opens with a list of rations including 40 grams of butter and 100 grams of ground beef that Valentine doubts exists locally.
Even cats, dogs and rats were gone from the city.
